question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a generic per-agent plugin configuration contract or as a narrower memory-wiki per-agent vault mechanism?
rationale: Both shapes can address the immediate shared-vault problem, but they create different plugin API, config compatibility, SecretRef, doctor, and security-boundary obligations that should not be chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Approve generic per-agent plugin config
options.body: Add a documented `agents.list[].plugins.entries` override/merge contract and implement memory-wiki on top of that shared plugin API direction.

options.title: Approve memory-wiki-only vault scoping
options.body: Add a narrower agent-aware vault mode or path-template mechanism inside memory-wiki and explicitly defer the broader plugin-config issue.

options.title: Document separate gateways only
options.body: Decline shared-gateway vault isolation for now and document separate gateway processes as the supported isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve generic per-agent plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a documented `agents.list[].plugins.entries` override/merge contract and implement memory-wiki on top of that shared plugin API direction.

likelyOwner.reason: Local blame ties the current memory-wiki registration and agent config schema to this person, and the decision spans config and plugin architecture.
